name: Owen McDonald
caption: The promotion's own elderly ring announcer and on-air president, a Northwest wrestling lifer who fronted the Grapplearium from its first card through its 1997 relaunch.

tenures.source: the promotion's own broadcasts, from its first card through its September 1997 relaunch prospectus

name: Eugene Curtis
caption: Play-by-play announcer on the promotion's debut broadcast, paired with color man Larry "The Chainsaw" Gaines.

name: Larry "The Chainsaw" Gaines
caption: Billed as a Northwest wrestling legend, he called color on the promotion's debut broadcast alongside Eugene Curtis.

name: "5150" John Doe
caption: Won the opening match of the promotion's first broadcast, advancing in its debut tournament.

name: Francis Quincy Cleveland
caption: A snobbish Beverly Hills-billed wrestler who lost the opening match of the promotion's debut broadcast and challenged for a rematch on the spot.

name: The Warden
caption: A rookie wrestler whose debut-broadcast bout against Hollywood Johnny Dreamer ended in a double-pinfall draw.

identity.note: The ring name is a generic prison-themed gimmick shared with two unrelated wrestlers under this name at other promotions, years apart with no roster or host overlap; recorded distinct.

name: "Hollywood" Johnny Dreamer
caption: A veteran technician whose debut-broadcast bout against The Warden ended in a double-pinfall draw.

name: The Witch King
caption: A robed, throne-sitting entrant in the promotion's debut tournament who cut a videotaped promo boasting of world titles held elsewhere before his first Grapplearium bout.

name: Thorn
caption: The promotion's Television Champion by late 1996, a Detroit-billed powerhouse who retained the title in the Grapplearium's November 1996 main event before later losing the Columbia Valley Championship to Drago.

tenures.source: the promotion's own 10 November 1996 and 28 January 1997 broadcasts

identity.note: The bare ring name is shared with several unrelated wrestlers billed under fuller "Thorn"-family names at other promotions; recorded distinct, no roster or host overlap.

name: "Master Of Pain" Barry Hart
caption: A Butte, Montana-billed comedy heel who challenged for the Television Championship in November 1996, losing when a moment of showboating cost him the pinfall.

tenures.source: The CWO's own Rankings record, period ending 12 January 1997 (/promotions/cwo/the wing's own served documents.

tenures.note: Billed from Butte, Montana at 6'3" and 245 pounds as the Master of Pain and the Ass Man, the Innovator of Rest Holds, with his 400-pound bodyguard Slabuu. On the card: won at Torture Chamber 2 (26 October 1997) against Cain Superstes. The page pairs Barry Hart and Mark Cutter: Hart attacks the returning Cutter in the ring ("Bounty collected. I told you not to mess with me and now it is even worse."). The page pairs Barry Hart and Slabuu: Slabuu is Hart's 400-pound bodyguard ("His 400 pound bodyguard, Slabuu"). The page pairs Barry Hart and Jason Knight: booked for the United States Championship under Softcore rules ("Barry Hart will be facing Jason Knight for the US Championship").

identity.note: Exact-name collision with records elsewhere; no document of this fed ties any of them to it. Kept distinct under the no-merge default, open to a merge on evidence.

name: Johnny "Cool" Coles
caption: Won a return bout on the November 1996 Grapplearium card after a prior absence from the promotion.

identity.note: The identical name is also carried by an untenured newsgroup year-end poll placing tagged to an unrelated federation, and by a separately tenured record at another promotion beginning several months later; no roster, host or date overlap ties either to this appearance.

name: Soul Skinner
caption: Lost a November 1996 Grapplearium bout to Johnny "Cool" Coles.

name: Iron Head Harley
caption: One half of the Devil's Disciples, the promotion's Tag Team Champions through late 1996.

name: Chopper Davidson
caption: One half of the Devil's Disciples, scoring the pinfall that retained their Tag Team Championship in November 1996.

name: Steve "Crusher" Kingston
caption: One half of Crusher Tech, a Boston-billed brawling tag team that challenged for the Tag Team Championship in November 1996 and won it early in 1997, later regaining it at Spring Showdown.

tenures.source: the promotion's own 10 November 1996 and 18 May 1997 broadcasts

name: Mark "Tech" Stephens
caption: One half of Crusher Tech, a Boston-billed technical-brawling tag team that challenged for the Tag Team Championship in November 1996 and won it early in 1997, later regaining it at Spring Showdown.

tenures.source: the promotion's own 10 November 1996 and 18 May 1997 broadcasts

name: "Hardcore" Matt Harris
caption: Debuted at the Grapplearium in November 1996 billed simply as Hardcore Harris; went on to become the promotion's Television Champion and, by Spring Showdown 1997, its World Heavyweight Champion.

tenures.source: the promotion's own 10 November 1996 debut and 18 May 1997 broadcast; billed only as "Hardcore Harris" at his debut, later under his full name

notes: The community's own year-end poll separately credits a wrestler of this name with winning three different federations' World titles in 1997, PCW among them.

name: "Cool" Chris Courage
caption: Lost his November 1996 Grapplearium debut to Hardcore Harris.

name: Christian Kingsworth
caption: Debuted at the Grapplearium in November 1996 and, by the promotion's own repeated later billing, won its World Heavyweight Championship at Birthday Brawl in January 1997 before vacating it.

tenures.source: the promotion's own 10 November 1996 broadcast; a rival federation's own March 1997 interview quoting his vacating the title

name: Iceman
caption: Lost a November 1996 Grapplearium bout to Christian Kingsworth by countout after an outside fan interfered on Kingsworth's behalf.

identity.note: A generic ring name shared with several unrelated wrestlers at other promotions; no roster, host or date overlap ties any of them to this appearance.

name: Gary Grayson
caption: One half of Sin & Salvation at the Grapplearium in November 1996; billed by 1997 under a singles gimmick, "American Nightmare" Gary Grayson, as a Columbia Valley Championship challenger.

tenures.source: the promotion's own 10 November 1996 and 18 May 1997 broadcasts

name: Caleb Temple
caption: One half of Sin & Salvation, submitting Nibs of Gangsta's Paradise with the Last Rites in November 1996.

identity.note: The identical name is separately attested at another promotion beginning three years later; too great a gap to connect on the name alone.

name: Skeetah
caption: One half of Gangsta's Paradise, defeated by Sin & Salvation in November 1996.

name: Nibs
caption: One half of Gangsta's Paradise, submitted by Caleb Temple's Last Rites in November 1996.

name: "King of Excuses" Kevin Jade
caption: Lost a chaotic November 1996 Grapplearium comedy bout to Dr. D-Day, with Iron Man Jack Kelly interfering against him at ringside.

name: Dr. D-Day
caption: Defeated Kevin Jade with his finisher, the Landmine, on the November 1996 Grapplearium card.

name: T.R. Ela
caption: A two-time former Television Champion who lost a steel-cage match to Ultimate Maniac in November 1996; both men shook hands afterward.

name: Ultimate Maniac
caption: A former Television Champion and former member of the Den of Destruction who beat T.R. Ela in a November 1996 steel-cage match by reaching the floor first.

name: Isaac Irvine
caption: Color commentator on the promotion's November 1996 broadcast, working alongside Scott Gaines.

name: Scott Gaines
caption: Play-by-play announcer on the promotion's November 1996 broadcast, distinct from wrestler Gunnar "The Grizzly" Gaines.

tenures.source: the promotion's own 10 November 1996 and 2 January 1997 broadcasts

name: Drago
caption: The promotion's Columbia Valley Champion through the first half of 1997, retaining the title against The Prophet at New Year's Bash and against Thorn at Birthday Brawl before eventually losing it to The Extremist.

tenures.source: the promotion's own 2 and 28 January 1997 broadcasts

identity.note: A different, unrelated "Dragon" ring name is billed on the promotion's own 1998 GeoCities successor of the same acronym, a wing this record's own promotion is not continuous with; no relation.

name: The Prophet
caption: Challenged Drago for the Columbia Valley Championship at New Year's Bash in January 1997 and lost.

identity.note: The identical ring name is separately attested at another promotion two months later and in an untenured newsgroup poll placing tagged to that same other promotion; no evidence ties either to this appearance.

name: "Iron Man" Jack Kelly
caption: Interfered against Kevin Jade in November 1996 and, by 1997, wrestled Barry Hart in the promotion's own tag ranks before entering the three-way World Heavyweight Championship match at Spring Showdown.

tenures.source: the promotion's own 10 November 1996 and 18 May 1997 broadcasts

identity.note: The "Iron Man" prefix is a common gimmick shared with several unrelated wrestlers at other promotions; no overlap ties any of them to this record.

name: Malachite
caption: One half of Negaforce, the DPW tag team that lost its title to Bigger Than Hollywood in the promotions' unification match at the Grapplearium in April 1997.

name: Jedite
caption: One half of Negaforce, the DPW tag team that lost its title to Bigger Than Hollywood in the promotions' unification match at the Grapplearium in April 1997.

tenures.source: the promotion's own 11 April 1997 broadcast; billed as Malachite's partner on the promotion's own card

name: The Extremist
caption: Won the Columbia Valley Championship in April 1997 and defended it into the summer, including a No Contest against Gary Grayson at Spring Showdown.

tenures.source: the promotion's own April and 18 May 1997 broadcasts

identity.note: An untenured newsgroup year-end poll placing under the identical ring name is tagged to an unrelated federation seven years later; no evidence ties it to this record.

name: "Maniac" Joe Colosi
caption: The promotion's Television Champion at Spring Showdown in May 1997, retaining the title against Dimension.

name: Dimension
caption: Challenged "Maniac" Joe Colosi for the Television Championship at Spring Showdown in May 1997 and lost.

name: Jak Martin
caption: Credited by the community's own corroborating record with taking the World Heavyweight Championship from "Hardcore" Matt Harris around July 1997, the same day he also defended another federation's own World Title.

tenures.source: the community own year-end poll and a crossover storyline documented at another federation, grade user-attested
